design_detail: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-person laboratory study with an ascending-dose ('run-up') design: 12 healthy adults with hallucinogen experience received, in up to 11 day-long sessions, placebo, two doses of triazolam (an active sedative comparator) and rising single doses of dextromethorphan until a stop point; the order of the three drug types was counterbalanced, but doses within each drug always rose. Physiological, psychomotor, observer-rated and self-rated effects were measured repeatedly during each session, hallucinogen and mystical-experience questionnaires at the end of each session, and persisting effects at a follow-up visit about one month after the last session. Sessions took place in a living-room-like setting with eyeshades and music after preparatory meetings, following safety guidelines for hallucinogen research.
can_establish: In these 12 screened, prepared, hallucinogen-experienced people in a supportive laboratory, how high single doses of dextromethorphan compare with placebo and triazolam in physiological, psychomotor and subjective effects over a session, how long psychomotor impairment lasted within the session, and what participants reported about the sessions a month later.
cannot_establish: Any effect on the day after a session (nothing was measured then), effects of over-the-counter products containing other ingredients, effects outside a supportive and supervised setting or in people without hallucinogen experience, whether effects depend on dose order (doses always rose), and whether the persisting effects reported at one month came from dextromethorphan rather than from the setting, triazolam sessions or expectation.

sample.recruitment: Not described in this report beyond paid volunteers with a history of hallucinogen use studied at Johns Hopkins.
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Medically and psychologically healthy, with a history of hallucinogen use; excluded for DSM-IV-TR substance dependence (other than nicotine or caffeine), pregnancy or nursing, significant medical conditions, contraindications to sedatives or anaesthetics, or a personal or immediate-family history of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, delusional, paranoid or schizoaffective disorder.
sample.demographics: Mean age 27.5 (range 20 to 40); 10 white, 1 African American, 1 Asian American. All had used LSD (median 10 lifetime uses) and psilocybin (mean 21); 7 had used dextromethorphan (1 to 10 uses), 3 PCP or ketamine, 8 Salvia divinorum and 6 MDMA.
sample.attrition: All 12 completed placebo, both triazolam conditions and at least four dextromethorphan conditions; higher doses were given until a stop point. Subjective data were missing for stop-point sessions, so peak subjective effects at each person's maximum dose could not be computed; the final monitor-rating questionnaire was used for 10 participants.
sample.selection_effects: Experienced, screened volunteers who knew the laboratory's psilocybin research and were prepared over two meetings; people with psychotic or bipolar illness in themselves or close family were excluded, so the sample under-represents those most at risk of adverse psychological reactions.

exposure.measurement: Doses given by the investigators in identical opaque capsules under double-blind conditions; participants were told they could receive placebo or any of 17 drugs from several classes.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions: single oral doses of dextromethorphan (free base) of 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700 and 800 mg/70 kg in ascending order, triazolam 0.25 and 0.5 mg/70 kg in ascending order, and lactose placebo, one condition per session, sessions at least 48 hours apart; drug-type order counterbalanced. Highest dextromethorphan dose reached: 400 mg/70 kg (n = 2), 500 (2), 600 (4), 700 (2), 800 (2); two people received all doses. Escalation stopped if the person could not complete a psychomotor and a computer task at any time point, or if the participant or investigator judged a higher dose inadvisable. Measures before dosing and at 30 to 360 minutes (vital signs and psychomotor tasks at 120, 240 and 360 minutes); end-of-session questionnaires about 7 hours after dosing; follow-up about one month after the last session, with a 25 mg dextromethorphan dose and 8-hour urine collection for CYP2D6 phenotyping. Vomiting: none after placebo, triazolam, 100 or 200 mg/70 kg; 2 of 12 after 300; 6 of 12 at 400, 2 of 10 at 500, '3 or 6' at 600, 1 of 3 at 700 and 2 of 2 at 800 mg/70 kg (7 of 12 at 400 or more); vomiting typically began 90 minutes or more after the capsules. At the maximum dose, systolic and diastolic pressure rose by 20.8 and 14.6 mm Hg and heart rate by 26 beats/min; the 0.5 mg/70 kg triazolam dose raised heart rate by 10.2 beats/min.
exposure.polysubstance: Participants were asked to use no drugs other than non-prescription pain relievers, tobacco and caffeine during the study; urine tested for cocaine, benzodiazepines and opioids and breath for alcohol before each session.
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Negative urine screens for cocaine, benzodiazepines and opioids and a negative breathalyser before each session (cannabis and other hallucinogens were not tested).

comparison.controls: The same participants' placebo session and triazolam sessions (an active sedative comparator).
comparison.matching: Within-person; drug-type order counterbalanced; doses within a drug ascending, not randomized.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable to within-person comparisons; prior experience and expectations about hallucinogens were not measured as covariates.

outcomes.instruments: Blood pressure and heart rate; Balance (seconds standing on one foot, eyes closed) and Circular Lights (hand-eye coordination); a 16-item monitor rating questionnaire; a 36-item self-rated subjective effects questionnaire; a Pharmacological Class Questionnaire (18 classes); the Mysticism Scale; the States of Consciousness Questionnaire (43 mystical-experience items); the Hallucinogen Rating Scale; an end-of-session 'like the experience' rating; at one month, a 143-item Persisting Effects Questionnaire and three questions on meaning, spiritual significance and well-being. Cognitive measures were taken but reserved for another paper.
outcomes.validity_norms: The mystical-experience and hallucinogen scales are validated for psilocybin; the authors note that few studies have examined how specific these measures are for hallucinogens against other drugs.
outcomes.operationalization: Peak effect as the maximum (or, for the psychomotor tasks, the minimum) value after dosing; a 'complete' mystical experience as at least 60% on six States of Consciousness scales; psychomotor tasks scored zero when the person was too impaired to do them.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None; dozens of items and scales were each compared with placebo (Fisher's LSD), with planned comparisons at each time point.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Monitors and participants blind to condition; blinding integrity not formally assessed, but the class questionnaire shows that most participants recognised active drug conditions.

analysis.effect_sizes: Mixed-effects regression (SAS Proc Mixed) with Fisher's LSD comparisons against placebo; means and SEMs only, no standardized effects or intervals. End-of-session liking (0 to 4): 1.25 (SEM 0.28) after placebo against 2.58 (0.38) at the penultimate and 2.83 (0.37) at the maximum dextromethorphan dose. Hallucinogen Rating Scale intensity 0.31 after placebo against 3.08 at the maximum dose; Mysticism Scale total 70.8 against 230.8 of 288. Peak self-rated drug effect 15.5 after placebo against 97.4 at the penultimate dose (0 to 100). Classic hallucinogen chosen on the class questionnaire by 91.7% at the maximum dose, and dissociative anaesthetic by 0%. 'Complete' mystical experience in 7 of 11 at the maximum dose and 2 of 11 at the penultimate dose. Physiological and psychomotor peaks are in an online supplementary table that was not read.
analysis.selective_reporting: Cognitive measures were collected but deferred to a separate publication; peak cardiovascular and psychomotor values and persisting-effect scores are only in supplementary tables.
analysis.power: Not addressed; 12 participants, fewer at the highest doses (10, 8, 4 and 2 at the top four dose levels).

interpretation_gap.results_show: High single doses of dextromethorphan raised blood pressure and heart rate, impaired balance and coordination for longer than triazolam (still present at the last in-session test at each person's two highest doses), caused vomiting in most people at the higher doses, and produced hallucinogen-like, mystical-type and liked experiences in these experienced volunteers; triazolam produced sedation. At one month, participants reported positive persisting changes and no lasting distress, without the questionnaire being able to separate dextromethorphan from triazolam sessions.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract says drug effects "resolved without significant adverse effects by the end of the session" and that high doses resembled psilocybin. Gaps: (1) psychomotor deficits were still present at the last psychomotor test of the session, and no psychomotor test was given at the end-of-session time; 'resolved' therefore rests on unmeasured recovery; (2) vomiting in most people at the higher doses and complete task failure at the highest doses are adverse effects the abstract's wording does not convey; (3) the similarity to psilocybin is a comparison across studies, with expectancy acknowledged by the authors; (4) the positive one-month effects are attributed to the sessions in general and to dextromethorphan only through informal interviews.

timeline.event: This study: the first controlled study of the effects of high doses of dextromethorphan, by the authors' account; a correction was published (Psychopharmacology volume 228, page 513), which was not read.

replication.where_it_stands: The only controlled study of high-dose dextromethorphan read for the library; it says nothing about the day after a session. Case reports of dependence and withdrawal after heavy long-term use are listed separately on the evidence map.

funding.declared_conflicts: Lawrence Carter is an employee of Jazz Pharmaceuticals and owns stock options in the company; no other disclosures. The study was conducted in compliance with United States laws.
funding.affiliations_note: Johns Hopkins psychedelic research group (Griffiths, Johnson), which also ran the psilocybin studies the participants knew about.

what_would_settle_it: A randomized-order, placebo-controlled study of dextromethorphan doses that people use, including over-the-counter combination products, with psychomotor and driving-related tests repeated until return to baseline and on the next day, sleep and mood measured over the following days, and a sample with and without hallucinogen experience.

domains.note: Drug-type order was counterbalanced, but doses within each drug always rose, so dose is confounded with session order and growing familiarity.
Single doses with a washout between sessions (exposure field); learning and expectation could build across the ascending sequence.
Double-blind capsules, but active conditions were readily recognised and participants expected hallucinogens; preparation, music and monitors were part of every session.
Missing subjective data at stop-point sessions prevented peak calculations at each person's maximum dose; fewer people at the highest doses; the final monitor questionnaire covered 10 participants.
Most outcomes are self-ratings or monitor ratings vulnerable to expectancy; psychomotor and cardiovascular measures are objective.
No registration; cognitive results deferred to another paper; many items compared without correction.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: High because dose order was not randomized, so dose effects are confounded with sequence; expectancy and the supportive setting further limit the subjective findings. The comparisons of each dose with the placebo session at the same time point are less affected than the dose-response pattern. May be cited for the profile and in-session time course of effects of high single doses under these conditions, for vomiting and cardiovascular effects, and for the one-month reports as reports; not for safety outside this setting, nor for anything about the next day.

key_findings.finding: Twelve healthy adults (9 men, mean age 27.5) with LSD and psilocybin experience took part; 7 had used dextromethorphan recreationally before. All received placebo, both triazolam doses and at least four dextromethorphan doses; seven stopped escalating because of significant behavioural impairment, two because the investigator judged higher doses inadvisable and one because the participant would not want that dose again.
key_findings.locator: Materials and Methods › Participants; Results, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: Time course: effects were generally significant by the first post-dose test, maximal over the next tests and lessening by the last; dextromethorphan impaired balance and hand-eye coordination for longer than triazolam, and at each person's penultimate and maximum doses the deficits were still present at the last psychomotor test of the session; the highest doses sometimes made the tasks impossible.
key_findings.locator: Results › Time-course of drug effects; Figure 1 legend

key_findings.finding: Dextromethorphan raised systolic and diastolic blood pressure with dose and raised heart rate at the two highest doses (by 20.8 and 14.6 mm Hg and 26 beats/min at each person's maximum); triazolam slightly lowered systolic pressure.
key_findings.locator: Results › Peak effects › Blood pressure and heart rate

key_findings.finding: Vomiting: no one vomited after placebo, triazolam or the two lowest dextromethorphan doses; 2 of 12 vomited at the third dose level and 7 of 12 at the fourth level or above (onset times in the exposure field).

Self-ratings: both drugs raised sedation-type items (drug effect, mentally slowed, unsteady, confused, blurred vision, good and bad effects); only dextromethorphan raised stimulation, dizziness, jitteriness, numbness and tingling, nervousness, nausea, flushing, restlessness, talkativeness, headache, liking and disliking; only triazolam raised sleepiness. Monitors rated dextromethorphan as raising distance from ordinary reality, visual effects, joy, nausea or vomiting, psychological discomfort, anxiety and, at the maximum dose, confusion and unresponsiveness.
key_findings.locator: Results › Monitor ratings; Participant ratings of subjective effects; Table 1

key_findings.finding: At the end of sessions, 11 of 12 identified the fourth dose level and their maximum dose as a classic hallucinogen; liking of the experience rose to 2.83 (SEM 0.37) at the maximum dose against 1.25 (0.28) after placebo (0 to 4); 7 of 11 met criteria for a 'complete' mystical-type experience at their maximum dose, none after placebo, triazolam or the three lowest doses.
key_findings.locator: Results › Pharmacological Class Questionnaire; End of session rating; Measures of mystical experience; Tables 2 and 3

key_findings.finding: About one month after the last session, participants endorsed positive persisting changes (attitudes, mood, social effects, behaviour, spirituality) at 46% to 61% of maximum scores, with low negative ratings; 4 of 12 rated the session experiences among the five most meaningful of their lives and 7 of 12 among the five most spiritually significant, and all 12 reported increased well-being. The questionnaire could not separate dextromethorphan from triazolam sessions; in unstructured interviews participants attributed the effects to sessions they thought were a classic hallucinogen.
key_findings.locator: Results › Measures assessed 1 month after drug administration › Persisting Effects Questionnaire, 1st to 3rd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: After sessions: one participant reported a headache after a session, attributed it to dextromethorphan and chose to stop; the primary monitor was reachable by phone throughout the study, but no volunteer called or reported distress after sessions, and no lasting distress or persisting perceptual phenomena were reported at the one-month follow-up.

The authors caution that participants knew the laboratory's psilocybin research and may have expected psilocybin, that expectancy, preparation, social support and the setting may have shaped the hallucinogen-like and positive ratings, and that the comparison with psilocybin is across studies.

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract says drug effects resolved without significant adverse effects by the end of the session, but the Results report balance and coordination deficits still present at the last psychomotor test at the two highest doses each person took, and the end-of-session time point included only questionnaires; vomiting occurred in 7 of 12 at the higher doses.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Abstract › Results; Results › Time-course of drug effects; Results › Emesis
reporting_issues.consequence: The study does not show when impairment ended; 'resolved' should not be cited as a finding.

reporting_issues.issue: The vomiting counts at the two highest dose levels use denominators (6 and 3, with '3 or 6' evidently a typo) that differ from the numbers who received those doses in Table 2 (8 and 4; values in the exposure field).
reporting_issues.consequence: Vomiting rates at the highest doses cannot be stated exactly; the overall 7 of 12 is unaffected.

reporting_issues.issue: The Data Analysis section gives the range of penultimate doses in mg/kg where the rest of the paper uses mg/70 kg.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Materials and Methods › Data Analysis, 1st paragraph
reporting_issues.consequence: Unit typo; the doses are per 70 kg.

reporting_issues.issue: The PMC page states that the article has been corrected (Psychopharmacology volume 228, page 513) but gives no link to the correction, which was not read.
reporting_issues.consequence: Values on this card come from the author manuscript; the correction should be checked before claims are verified.

reporting_issues.issue: The final version of the monitor rating questionnaire was developed after the study began and used for the 10 participants enrolled thereafter.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Materials and Methods › Monitor rating questionnaire
reporting_issues.consequence: Monitor-rated outcomes rest on 10 of 12 participants.
